answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake at one entry wharf before it can transact: each signed pulse of recent useful work releases a small slice of earning rights, while dormant or duplicated identities earn nothing. A sybil operator must fund a separate stake per clone and keep each one producing real work, so cloning 1,000 identities costs 1,000 stakes plus constant compute, while one honest agent pays once. Like a cedar, reputation grows slowly: the longer an identity behaves well, the more weight its attestations carry.
